Definition: from G303 and G71; to lead up; by extension to bring out; specially, to sail away:--bring (again, forth, up again), depart, launch (forth), lead (up), loose, offer, sail, set forth, take up.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to lead up, to bring out, and most often to set sail: Paul and his company loosed from Paphos and came to Perga, and Jesus went into a ship with His disciples and said, 'Let us go over unto the other side of the lake,' and they launched forth. It is the word for a journey beginning — a ship leaving harbour, a prisoner brought up before a court, a sacrifice led up to the altar.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for setting sail carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the going — Paul leaving Paphos for Perga, and Jesus launching out with His disciples into the storm.
